text: Refines D-0316 and D-0321 for #610, step 5 of #564's plan: configured Go acceptance is admitted by default, through the Go adapter, in public planning and in builds, and an explicit trusted Go adapter still overrides it. Planning runs a draft's tests on the independent captured commit and needs exactly one matching completed eligible failure per full identity, a test failure or a proposed production API compiler failure. A passing, skipped, absent, unfinished, duplicate or mismatched selection blocks the draft; ordinary build and suite failures let independent selections continue without supplying evidence; install, startup, transport, cleanup, deadline and cancellation failures veto it, and every selector's status and reason survives clipped feedback. Candidates need every applicable captured command and exactly one fresh runtime pass per selector, with execution identities, staged acceptance and declared dependency-input bytes checked before preparation. Builder staging admits only planned changes and new Go regressions, and candidate configuration, replaced locks, diagnostics, compile success and Accepted booleans supply no authority or completion. The builder and planner tools, both queues, fresh final checks and final proposal validation apply the same rules under one run deadline and test allowance, and failed final checks block review and readiness. pytest, Vitest, Jest, mixed unsupported plans and configured legacy acceptance are refused before preparation, without migration; command-only checks, unconfigured legacy Go, and existing hashes and locks are unchanged, and external intake stays disabled. A Go part with no installation may declare only a dependency-free go.mod and an optional empty go.sum, sealed offline. The merger ran the configured-Go pinned-image opt-in and the prepared Docker Go suite on linux/arm64 before merging.
